labels.label: btzthm:BTZ_Cauchy-completness
labels.notes: Row partial and unmarked (module docstring has no **`label`** mark); correct, since (i) => (iii) is absent and the E0 scope and the OQ-142 (e)(f)/OQ-150/OQ-152 readings (all OPEN) are in force. iii_imp_ii: an IsMaximal GHExt that satisfies CauchyCompleteMaximal witnesses the existential. Trivial, matching the paper's 'trivial'. IsMaximal is unused, as disclosed. ii_imp_i: (exists X : GHExt M, E0C1CauchyComplete X.N and IsE0CauchyMaximal X.N) -> GH, MGH and IsCauchyComplete 2 of e0RegMFlat M. The hypotheses on M are T2, connected, ChartedSpace E0Y and HasGroupoid. GH of M and second countability are dropped (they appear nowhere in the signature, checked by #check), which makes the theorem stronger. Connectedness is added and disclosed (OQ-150 (b)). The paper's BTZ-extension (l.325) carries no GH requirement, and GHExt adds (CE N).GloballyHyperbolic. In the library's vocabulary that is a hypothesis added to (ii), so it weakens (ii) => (i). Under the paper's l.222 definition (GH means a Cauchy surface exists), E0C1CauchyComplete, which contains a Cauchy surface, implies it, and prop_reg_complete' (strict, already audited) takes the same GH argument. The docstring checklist (marked with a warning) and the REPORT's questions both disclose it and name the missing lemma (a Cauchy surface implies ETT GH for E0-manifolds). The disclosure is honest and the row is partial, so this is not major. See the minor finding on the wording. iii_imp_i is the composite. The isometry lemmas are proved for arbitrary data and are not vacuous. regMap is defined as an honest subtype restriction. isLocalIsometry_regMap goes through liftPropOn_iff_repOn and e0_flat_transition_aux. surjective_regMap uses (range ι)ᶜ ⊆ S0 and mem_S0_iff. Each transport lemma (IsCauchyComplete with all four fields via an explicit isometry of induced length spaces, MGH via composition of Cauchy embeddings, GH via the lean-causal lemma) has non-trivial hypotheses that are satisfiable. Findings: l.1593 '(ii) => (i) is a consequence of prop:reg_complete' is correctly a missing step, not an error. The paper's proposition concludes for Reg N, and the transfer to Reg M along the induced flat isometry is left implicit. The remark that M's standing GH is unused is true. The confirmation that '(iii) => (ii) is trivial' is true.

findings.what: The checklist row for (ii) calls the carried global hyperbolicity of the extension 'a reading, not an added hypothesis of the paper'. In Lean it is an added hypothesis of (ii) => (i): the paper's BTZ-extension (l.325) has no GH clause, and nothing in the library derives ETT's GH from E0C1CauchyComplete. It is redundant only under the paper's l.222 definition, and that redundancy is unproved. The row also cites 'OQ-142 (a)' for the GH-target extension, but OQ-142 (a) concerns the a.e.-morphism reading; the GHExt shape comes from OQ-150 (a) / T-btz-maximal-extension. The REPORT's 'questions' entry states the matter correctly.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'added in Lean: the target is globally hyperbolic (ETT GH). Redundant under the paper's l.222 definition, since E0C1CauchyComplete supplies a Cauchy surface, but the lemma Cauchy surface => GH for E0-manifolds is not in the library.' Fix the OQ citation, and when curating, record this beside OQ-142/OQ-152 as an open item rather than as a settled reading.
